messages.subject: factor scores calculation
parts:
Hello,
I have a dataset with missing values and both binary and continous variable. I suppose there is one latent varaible underlying these. How can I calculate manually score using residual covariance matrix, factor  loading matrix... I'm interested on estimate the contribution of each variable in the model not only the score of the latent one.  

fit1<-sem(Mfa1, data=SEMdata, se="robust",ordered=ordered,missing="pairwise",estimator = "WLSMV" )  
lavPredict(fit1) #estimated values for the latent variaible

Thanks a lot 
Francesca

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: factor scores calculation
parts:
On 9/18/20 3:55 PM, Francesca Graziano wrote:
> I have a dataset with missing values and both binary and continous
> variable. I suppose there is one latent varaible underlying these. How
> can I calculate manually score using residual covariance matrix, factor
> loading matrix...

If your fitted object is called 'fit', then lavInspect(fit, "est") will
show all the (estimated) model matrices.

But it will not be trivial to compute the factor scores 'manually',
given that you have binary data. lavaan uses 'EBM' (Empirical Bayes
Modal) by default in this setting, and for each observation, the 'mode'
is found using numerical optimization. (ML is also available.)

The relevant code can be seen in the file 'lav_predict.R:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/master/R/lav_predict.R

in the function 'lav_predict_eta_ebm_ml()' (starting from line 1018). A
local function is defined (f.eta.i, producing the loglikelihood of the
items, for given values of the factors), and nlminb() is used to find
the 'scores' (=values for the factors) that maximize this loglikelihood
(ML), or the posterior (EBM).

Yves.
